title: Jobsite Housekeeping
summary: Poor housekeeping causes trips, falls, fires, and struck-by injuries, plus delays and damage. This talk covers keeping walkways clear, managing cords and waste, and protecting exits.
talking_points: Keep floors, walkways, and stairs dry, clean, and clear of waste and scrap.
Route hoses, power cords, and welding leads out of walkways and travel paths.
Keep material away from floor openings, roof edges, excavations, and trenches. Stack and store material where it cannot fall on anyone.
Do not let scrap or garbage pile up - remove unused material as you go.

Never block emergency exits, fire equipment, or first aid stations. Keep chemicals and gases away from heat sources and electrical equipment. Use separate covered containers for trash, oily rags, and flammable or hazardous waste.
site_hazards_to_check: Scrap, offcuts, sawdust, or debris built up in work areas and on stairs
Cords, hoses, and leads run across walkways
Material stacked near openings, edges, or trenches, or piled where it can topple
Blocked exits, fire extinguishers, or first aid stations
Oily rags or flammable waste in open or shared containers near heat
discussion_questions: Which walkways and stairs on this site are cluttered right now?
Where do cords and hoses cross paths, and how do we reroute them?
Are our exits and fire equipment clear and easy to reach?
